$comment: Single source for the participant card (CARD.md) and the hub (hub/index.html). Edit this file, then run npm run card. npm run card:check fails when the generated files are out of date. Plain English, one idea per sentence.
title: Workshop 5 · AI SRE first responder

start.say: Install Claude Code with the official instructions at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup, then create this isolated starter. Terminal 1 starts Claude Code before theory or edits; terminal 2 configures the SDK and runs the lab.

assistant.title: Claude Code first minutes
assistant.prompt: Read CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and CARD.md. Explain what we will build, why it helps the on-call team, and what evidence we need. Name the two starter exercises. Do not edit files or run approval, execution, mitigation, resolution, commit or push commands. Wait for my review.

start.see: ✓ SDK preflight passes before fault injection, then the lab runs. Hub: http://127.0.0.1:4320/hub · Console: http://127.0.0.1:4320 · Shop: http://127.0.0.1:4310.
start.check: `curl 127.0.0.1:4320/api/health` shows `"mode":"healthy"` and the selected model. `npm run model:check` must return READY before a real-model fault injection.
stuck: Port 4310 or 4320 is already in use
Another copy runs. Stop only your own workshop launcher with Ctrl+C in its terminal. Never kill an unknown process.
Install Node 22 or newer. Check with `node --version`.
The console header says no telemetry
Wait 20 seconds. The shop writes telemetry every few seconds while traffic runs.
Report the missing API/provider configuration. Use `npm start -- --fast --offline` only as an explicit fallback; it is not model evidence. See `docs/claude-code.md`.
start.why: Use an isolated local copy so you can break the demo without touching real customers or another participant's work.

cores.name: Investigate the evidence
cores.goal: Break the shop, let the console raise an incident, and check every claim in the diagnosis against the data. Find what the agent cannot see.
cores.slides: Core 1: Investigate the evidence · Core 1: Check the claims

steps.do: Break the shop once: click `Bad deploy v2.15.0` in the shop OR run `npm run chaos -- deploy v2.15.0 --mode bad-deploy` in your second terminal. Do not do both.
steps.see: After about one minute a new incident appears in the console sidebar. You did not open it; the deterministic listener did.
steps.stuck: No incident after three minutes: look at the lab terminal. Traffic must print requests. Started without `--fast`? Then detection takes five minutes.
steps.before: Telemetry is recorded service data. The listener opens an incident when server metrics cross a fixed limit; no model makes that decision.

steps.do: Open the incident. Read the banner at the top, then the diagnosis.
steps.see: The model output may vary. Expect missing deploy evidence, a verified tool trace and explicit data gaps; the starter cannot see the deploy.
steps.check: Preserve the diagnosis and trace. Verify every cited reference in `demo/data/telemetry.json`, then search that file for `v2.15.0`: there WAS a deploy outside the starter's visible tool result.
steps.stuck: References are text, not links. Search the file for the timestamp.
steps.before: An evidence reference points to an observation. A data gap means unknown, not proof that nothing happened.

steps.do: Challenge the agent in chat: Could this be something other than the deployment?
steps.see: Real output may vary. With the explicit offline fallback, the agent returns a scripted summary; that is not a new model investigation.
steps.check: Compare the answer with `ruled_out`, the trace and the data gap. If it fabricates a deploy citation or fails the contract, preserve the output and stop; do not call it success or weaken the contract.
steps.stuck: Chat refuses your sentence: that is correct for anything that changes the system. Approve, execute and resolve are buttons.
steps.before: Free-text chat is not checked by the structured verdict contract. Verify its claims manually against telemetry and trace; use Investigate for a contract-validated diagnosis.

steps.do: Save the diagnosis in `docs/diagnosis-live.md`. Then record what you checked: `npm run progress:note -- "Core 1: <what you verified>"`
steps.see: One new line at the bottom of `PROGRESS.md`.
steps.check: Your note names the references you checked, not only that you did it.
steps.stuck: Do not approve. There is nothing safe to execute yet. Core 2 gives the agent its eyes back.
steps.before: A progress note records a check you performed. It is history, not a test result by itself.

cores.why: A plausible explanation is not permission to change a service. Find the missing signal before proposing a fix.
cores.proof: A saved diagnosis with checked references and the list_deploys data gap.

cores.name: Build a change safely and test it
cores.goal: Rebuild the read-only `list_deploys` tool test-first, prove it with the tests and the bench, and watch the diagnosis change.
cores.slides: Core 2: Build a change safely · Core 2: Prove it on the live incident

steps.do: Run the red test: `npx tsx --test test/workshop/tools.test.ts`. Ask Claude Code for a small plan, then wait for human review.
steps.see: The test fails: `list_deploys` returns nothing. `npm run bench` fails too: without deploys the agent misses the bad deploy.
steps.check: Read the failing assertion before you change code. Say in one sentence why it fails.
steps.stuck: Find the single `TODO(A5)` handler stub in `src/tools.ts`. Restore the read-only handler binding; inspect and preserve the existing MCP registration.
steps.before: A red test exposes the missing behaviour. The bench checks scripted outcomes across fixed scenarios, not model quality.

steps.do: Build the `list_deploys` handler in `src/tools.ts` with Claude Code or by hand. Keep the existing MCP registration intact.
steps.see: `test/workshop/tools.test.ts` is green. The A8 valid-approval executor assertion remains red until Core 3.
steps.check: After plan review, implement and run `npx tsx --test test/workshop/tools.test.ts`, then `npm run typecheck` and `npm run bench`. The bench prints `PASS bench`; executor tests remain intentionally red until Core 3 restores the approval gate.
steps.stuck: The tool still returns `[]`: inspect the handler binding and the preserved registration; do not add a second registration.
steps.before: MCP exposes named tools. The existing registration points to a handler that reads data; restore that binding only after the human reviews the small plan.

steps.do: Save. In the same incident, ask in chat: `Investigate: customers report checkout errors`
steps.see: The lab terminal prints a console reload line. Inspect the new diagnosis, its observed trace, deploy references, data gaps and proposal; real model wording and actions can vary.
steps.check: Verify the actual trace and references against `demo/data/telemetry.json`. If the citation is fabricated or the contract fails, preserve the output and stop. Record what you verified: `npm run progress:note -- "Core 2: ..."`
steps.stuck: Incident gone? Incident history persists in SQLite, while the shop resets on restart. Do not restart the launcher to reload code; saving auto-reloads the console. For a fresh repeat, use a new disposable checkpoint copy; do not rebreak a stale incident.
steps.before: A trace records the tools used for a diagnosis. Re-investigation lets you compare the same incident before and after the repair.

cores.why: Core 1 found a deployment the agent cannot read. Repair that evidence path instead of guessing the cause.
cores.proof: Passing tool test, typecheck and bench; the same live incident now cites the deployment.

cores.name: Judge the recovery
cores.goal: Rebuild the approval gate, sign the rollback with your name, and decide from the recovery checks whether the incident may close.
cores.slides: Core 3: Judge the recovery · Core 3: Close it, or stop safely

steps.do: Run the red test: `npx tsx --test test/workshop/executor.test.ts`. Rebuild `checkApproval` in `src/executor.ts` (`TODO(A8)`).
steps.see: The test is green. The executor now refuses to act without a named approval for this incident and this proposal.
steps.check: Before a human approves the rollback, `npm run verify` and `npm run test:workshop` pass. The console reloads by itself.
steps.stuck: Read `test/workshop/executor.test.ts`. It names every case the gate must refuse.
steps.before: The approval gate validates a named human decision for this incident and proposal. The starter fails closed until you rebuild it.

steps.do: Open your incident and read the diagnosis and evidence. Type your name. Click Approve, then Execute rollback.
steps.see: The banner asks you to wait for execution and all three recovery checks. About two minutes later, inspect LANDED or NOT LANDED and the recovery table.
steps.check: The half check may fail. The full and double checks must both pass. On NOT LANDED the banner names the failed check, its value and the limit.
steps.stuck: A button is grey: the banner says which step is allowed now. The server refuses every other button.
steps.before: Rollback restores the prior deployment. Recovery checks capture measured values against a frozen limit; execution success alone is insufficient.

steps.do: LANDED: click Mark mitigated, then Resolve with notes. NOT LANDED: do not close. Read the failed check, then investigate in chat or escalate.
steps.see: After you resolve, the next-step detail says Resolved and directs you to the notes and lesson. Execute stays disabled.
steps.check: If resolved, `lessons/lessons.md` has your name and the incident id. If NOT LANDED, confirm the incident remains open and retain the failed check. Record your actual outcome: `npm run progress:note -- "Core 3: …"`
steps.stuck: Never execute again to get a green result. NOT LANDED is a correct, safe stop.
steps.before: LANDED means the full and double checks passed. Mitigated and resolved are separate human decisions. NOT LANDED or unknown means stop.

cores.why: The agent must not authorize its own action. A successful rollback is not proof that the service recovered.
cores.proof: Passing gate tests plus a justified human closure, or a documented NOT LANDED stop with the incident left open.

deeper.name: Write your team intent.md
deeper.do: Fill `intent.md`: who the agent serves, the boundary, and three checks a stranger can verify. The design-control-loop skill can interview you.

deeper.name: Read the contract
deeper.do: Write `docs/spec.md` for the evidence rules in `src/contract.ts`. Run `npx tsx --test test/contract.test.ts` and break one rule on purpose.

deeper.name: Add your own guard rule
deeper.do: Add one deny rule of your own to `.claude/hooks/guard.mjs` BY HAND (the agent may not edit hooks). Prove it with a deny line in `approvals/audit.jsonl`. Write `docs/decisions/D01-*.md`.

deeper.name: Add a bench case
deeper.do: Add one case to `bench/cases.json`, run `npm run bench`. Ask the agent to lower `bench/ratchet.json` and watch the guard deny it.

deeper.name: The git gate
deeper.do: Ask the agent to push `fix/<your-name>`: denied. Your neighbour runs `npm run approve:git -- <their-name> fix/<your-name> "<reason>"` in their own terminal.

deeper.name: Your hackathon intent.md
deeper.do: Write `docs/hackathon-intent.md` for the agent you build next. Hand off with the `/handoff` skill.

checkpoints.say: The committed-HEAD starter has the A5 tool exercise and a fail-closed A8 approval gate.
Core 2 retains the solved read-only tool and the fail-closed A8 approval gate.
Core 3 is the solved committed HEAD with no exercise cuts.

catchUp: Run `npm run checkpoint -- core-2` or `npm run checkpoint -- core-3` from any starter copy. Each creates a separate current-HEAD worktree under `.lab/checkpoints/` and refuses to overwrite an existing destination. Your files remain unchanged. Never copy runtime data, approvals, progress, or lesson history.
